steps.prompt: What is the job of “So, anyway, …” in a story?
options: It moves the story on to the next part.
It asks the listener a question.
steps.answer: It moves the story on to the next part.
steps.why: So, anyway takes the listener from the background to the next event.

steps.title: Telling a story, and reacting to one
steps.html:
What you are doingWhat you say
opening the storyYou’ll never believe what happened. / A funny thing happened this morning.
giving the backgroundI was on the train… It was a hot day…
moving it onSo, anyway, … / Then … / Suddenly …
closing itIn the end … / So it was all OK in the end.
reacting: surpriseYou’re joking! / Really!
reacting: sympathyOh no! That’s awful! / What a nightmare!
keeping it goingSo then what happened?

The background of a story is in the Past Continuous: I was sitting on the train…

The events are in the Past Simple: a woman put a box on the seat… the cat jumped out…

Reacting is not optional in English. If you say nothing, the other person thinks you are not interested.

Keep reactions short: Oh no! Really! You’re joking! So then what happened?

You will use the same reacting phrases again in Unit 6, Lesson 18, for good and bad news.

steps.title: Informal email · model
steps.html:
The same kind of story, written as an informal email. You will write your own at the end.

An email about a bad journey

Subject: You’ll never believe what happened

Dear Alina,

Guess what — I had the worst journey of my life last Tuesday.

I was sitting on the train to Astana, reading, when a woman put a large box on the seat next to me. Ten minutes later the box started to move. There was a cat inside it! It jumped out and ran down the carriage, and the woman looked at me angrily, as if it was my fault.

Anyway, in the end a young man caught it near the door and everyone laughed. I was so embarrassed.

What a nightmare. Write back soon and tell me about your week.

Marat

steps.title: Write an informal email about a journey that went wrong.
steps.sub: About 100–120 words. Follow the model: greeting, opening, background + event, ending, sign-off.
steps.html:
1. Plan (from the model): Dear … → Guess what / You’ll never believe what happened → where you were and what you were doing → what happened suddenly → Anyway, in the end … → Write back soon.
  • Dear …,
  • Guess what — …
  • I was … when …
  • Anyway, in the end …
  • What a nightmare. Write back soon.
  • (your name)
DearGuess whatYou’ll never believe what happenedI waswhenSuddenlySo, anywayIn the endWhat a nightmare.Write back soonembarrassedangrilynightmare
steps.modelHtml:
• I began with a greeting and ended with a sign-off.
  • I opened the story with a phrase from the Useful language box.
  • The background is in the Past Continuous and the events are in the Past Simple.
  • I used in the end to close the story.
  • I said how I felt.
